decision_rule.inputs: the v8 grid's rows for arms pointer-stable (C) and transcript-grow (A); estimator = quantile_ci(...,q=0.95) from experiments/ptr-engine/longrun/analyze_stats.py:187-247 with resamples=10000, seed=20261020 (PARM-1 frozen)
decision_rule.magnitude_gate_note: the 100 ms rep-level gate is a SCHEDULING predicate, not an adjudication threshold: it gates spending, never a verdict, and failing it asserts nothing about the model. It is set between the two measured gap families - 315.29 ms p50 / 530.0 ms p95 on rows-longrun-c vs 32.39 / 11.99 ms p50 and -2.35 / -57.65 ms p95 on rows-longrun-v3 / -v4 (docs/P95-POWER.md:127-131) - so an effect 10x smaller than the one claimed cannot promote a second tranche.
decision_rule.no_cross_era_comparison: rows-longrun-c is the v2-fixture era; the run this card prices is the v8 era. same_provenance() refuses a cross-fixture comparison by name (card 9f2e8259), so the 315.29 ms reference is quoted as the historical effect, never as a comparator in the rule.
decision_rule.step_0_admissibility: if either pair arm's usable_n < 60 -> H1 REFUSED with the estimator's own message; STOP, do not promote (S2)
decision_rule.step_1_P2_pooled: P2 := CI_C.hi < CI_A.lo on the pooled per-arm population (n=144) - PARM-1's frozen disjointness rule, in the C-lower direction
decision_rule.step_2_P1_recurrence: for each rep r in 1..3: d_r := p50_C(r) - p50_A(r). p50 at n=48 is admissible (n*(1-q)=24 >= 3) while p95 at n=48 is refused. P1 := all three d_r >= 100 ms
decision_rule.step_3_promote: promote iff P1 and P2 -> run tranche 2 (396 requests)
decision_rule.step_4_stop_no_replication: if not P2 -> STOP. Do NOT run the 792-request grid. Publish H1 as refused/null on this era and report that the C-grid effect did not recur.
decision_rule.step_5_hold_mixed: if P2 and not P1 -> HOLD: no tranche 2, no 792 grid, report the pooled separation as a single-grid result

question: Re-price the arm-comparison schedule against P95-POWER's measured power and say what the next 288-792 requests should buy.

recommendation.tranche_2: add 3 pair reps (288 turns / 396 requests) -> PAIR-6+CTX-2
recommendation.why: H1 separation is already reached at raw 48 on the only grid that shows the effect (100 % disjoint at 48/60/144, 254 ms observed margin: docs/P95-POWER.md:127-137), so turns are not what A* buys - runs are. The next requests must buy independent RUNS of the pair, not depth in a cell, and they must buy them inside a four-arm grid because PARM-1:150-152 defines the adjudicating grid that way. 3 pair reps is the smallest number that gives a between-run replication read plus 36 H3 pairs; 2 context reps is the smallest that lets B and D be estimated at all.

stop_rules_requests.rule: hard ledger ceiling: before any cell, remaining >= 264 (one 4-arm 48-turn cell at factor 1.374532). Tranche 1 + tranche 2 cap at 660 + 396 = 1,056 requests, leaving 2,163 of 3,219.
refuse to start tranche 2 unless remaining >= 396 (288 turns). At 1,767 left after the comfortable ceiling, still true; at <396 the tranche cannot be funded and H1 stays a one-grid result.
after exclusions (E1-E4), if either pair arm's usable n < 60 -> H1 refused, STOP; do not buy reps for a read that cannot print. At 3 reps the headroom is 84 exclusions per arm (58.3 %).
H3 veto on rep 1 (b+c >= 6 with exact two-sided p < 0.05 and C worse, or C loses more than 2 of 12 checkpoints) -> abandon the remaining 6 cells. Spent after 4 cells = 264; saves 396 of the 660.
either arm's grade_v5 decidable < 8 of 12 -> H3 unadjudicable (PARM-1:113); do not buy further reps (132 requests per arm-cell).
any turn wall_ms/1000 > 180 (--turn-wall-cap) is excluded, never retried past the cap; exclusion-induced n < 60 falls through to S2.
ATTACK or V-GATE-CHAIN reports a defect after the run starts -> halt at the next cell boundary, no further cells.
if tranche 1 stops for any of S2-S6, freeze spend and re-price on a new card; no automatic tranche 2, no fallback to the 792 grid.
